analysis.title: GS Callahan - GS US TMT drawdown (22 Nov 2026)
key_insights: NDX closed down 11% on the week, including a ~8% slide Thursday and Friday. It was a bottom-5 week in 20 years, led by Semis down 17%, the worst week for Semis since September 2011.
Cross-asset stress: Gold at 18-month lows, Copper falling sharply, and Nasdaq VIX (VXN) at its highest close since COVID. US Financial Conditions are at the tightest in more than 2 years.

Tech-heavy indices are oversold (NDX, SOX, Info Tech, S&P 500, R2K). Valuations are near 10-15 year lows, with NDX at 17x fwd P/E and SOX at about 12-13x. Callahan sees conditions for an oversold bounce.

Year-end rally optimism has faded despite firm fundamentals (firm compute prices, big beat/raise prints from KEYS, NVDA, PANW). Price action has hit risk appetite, with no identifiable catalyst and a buyers' strike plus rotational unwind.

The October pullback ahead of the Midterms has become a Semiconductor bear market by definition. Charts suggest AI/semis cuts are coming, but investors do not see that as a near-term catalyst, which makes buying harder.
NVDA is setting the tone: lower in 9 of 10 sessions, down 7 weeks in a row (-13% two weeks ago, -21% last week), and has shed $2.7T of market cap in 33 days.
Info Tech vs S&P 500 relative drawdown is the largest in 20+ years except 2013 (PC to smartphone transition). SOX is about 23% below its 200-dma, after being about 80% above it this spring.
SOX fwd P/E of 12-13x is at 15+ year lows despite a positive revision cycle.
Asset-light, non-China-exposed growth cyclicals (Live, Payments, Internet) have not traded better as a hedge to Semis, per Callahan's charts.

GIR's Eric Sheridan lists AMZN, UBER and SPCX as compelling risk/reward. His Amazon note projects Alexa for Shopping at ~$16bn+ in 2026 revenue and notes revenue per unit down ~220 bps y/y in 3Q26. His blue-sky AWS scenario is mid-50s y/y growth in 2027 and 2028 vs guidance of >40%.
GIR's Ben Snider sees three conditions for an S&P 500 correction bottom: improved AI earnings confidence, a dovish Fed signal, and a major decline in investor positioning.

GIR Memory team remains constructive on Samsung and Hynix, with ~20% shareholder return yields, despite lower forward OP estimates and price targets. Concerns are AI capex sustainability, muted phone/PC demand, and more China supply. MU fell about 25% last week.

GS Hedge Fund VIP basket (GSTHHVIP) lagged the S&P 500 by 14 pp over six months, rivaling its worst underperformance in 20 years. Apple is outperforming the NDX for the first time since the late-2022 ChatGPT launch.

Holiday-shortened week ahead: off-quarter earnings (ADI, ADSK, DELL, WDAY, NTNX, HPQ, ZM, HPE, SMTC), US Core PCE Wednesday, market closed Thursday, 1pm close Friday, then AWS re:Invent and the sellside conference circuit in early December.
